title: Non-approved substances
summary: Pharmacological substances that are not addressed elsewhere on the List and are not approved for human therapeutic use by a governmental health authority.
examples: Substances in pre-clinical or clinical development
Designer drugs without current approval for human therapeutic use
athleteNote: A product being sold online or described as a research chemical does not mean it is approved or safe for an athlete.

title: Anabolic agents
summary: This class includes anabolic-androgenic steroids and other agents with anabolic effects.
examples: Selected selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs), such as ostarine
athleteNote: Some products marketed for muscle-building may contain undeclared or prohibited ingredients. Check ingredients and official guidance before use.

title: Peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances
summary: This class covers specified peptide hormones, growth factors, related substances and mimetics.
examples: Growth hormone and its releasing factors
athleteNote: The Prohibited List defines which substances and related agents are included; this short overview is not a complete list.

title: Beta-2 agonists
prohibitedWhen: At all times, subject to specified exceptions
summary: Beta-2 agonists are medicines commonly used for respiratory conditions. The List prohibits this class, with specific exceptions and conditions for certain inhaled medicines.
examples: Some inhaled medicines have specific permitted-use conditions
athleteNote: Do not infer that an inhaler is permitted from its brand or route alone. Check the exact active ingredient and current List conditions with a qualified medical professional.

title: Hormone and metabolic modulators
summary: This class includes specified substances that affect hormone activity or metabolic processes.
athleteNote: The class contains different substances and exceptions. Check the current List rather than relying on a broad drug-family name.

title: Diuretics and masking agents
prohibitedWhen: At all times, subject to specified exceptions
summary: This class includes specified diuretics and other agents that can alter or obscure findings in a sample.
athleteNote: Some substances have route-specific exceptions, and some combinations have additional rules. Check the exact substance and current List.

title: Stimulants
prohibitedWhen: In-competition, subject to specified exceptions and thresholds
summary: The List prohibits specified stimulants during the in-competition period. Not every stimulant-like ingredient is prohibited.
athleteNote: Some substances have thresholds or specified exceptions, and some are monitored rather than prohibited. Check the current List and ask a qualified professional.

title: Narcotics
summary: The List prohibits specified narcotics during the in-competition period.
athleteNote: Never stop or change prescribed treatment without medical advice. Ask your doctor and anti-doping organization how the rules apply to your treatment.

title: Cannabinoids
summary: The List prohibits specified natural and synthetic cannabinoids during the in-competition period, with stated exceptions.
athleteNote: Products may contain ingredients not clearly shown on the label. Check current official guidance before using cannabinoid products.

title: Glucocorticoids
prohibitedWhen: In-competition for specified routes of administration
summary: Glucocorticoids are prohibited in-competition when administered by routes specified in the List, including oral, rectal and injectable routes.
athleteNote: Status depends on substance, route and timing. Discuss treatment with your doctor and check current washout and Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) guidance.

title: Beta-blockers
prohibitedWhen: In specified sports, in-competition and sometimes at all times
summary: Beta-blockers are prohibited only in the sports and circumstances identified in the Prohibited List.
athleteNote: Whether this class applies depends on your sport and competition context. Check the sport-specific section of the current List.

title: Manipulation of blood and blood components
summary: This class covers specified methods that manipulate blood or blood components to alter their use or transport.
examples: Administration or reintroduction of specified blood products
Specified methods that enhance oxygen transfer
athleteNote: The List defines the prohibited methods and permitted medical circumstances. Seek qualified advice if you have a medical procedure or concern.

title: Chemical and physical manipulation
summary: This class covers specified tampering, attempted tampering and prohibited intravenous infusions or injections.
examples: Tampering or attempted tampering with samples
Certain intravenous infusions or injections outside the permitted circumstances
athleteNote: Medical care and permitted procedures have specific rules and exceptions. Consult the current List and your anti-doping organization.

title: Gene and cell doping
summary: This class covers specified methods that use nucleic acids, gene editing or cells to alter performance.
examples: Specified gene editing or gene silencing methods
Use of cells to enhance performance by prohibited means
athleteNote: The Prohibited List describes the scope of these methods. This educational summary is not a substitute for the full List.
